stories.title: GRA to stand down planned industrial action
stories.summary: The Garda Representative Association is to stand down planned industrial action in the form of a work-to-rule which was due to commence tomorrow. It follows a meeting tonight of the GRA's Central Executive Committee. It voted to stand down the work-to-rule position for this week after making what it described as "significant progress with the Garda Commissioner". Members were planning to engage in five days of work-to-rule action this week which would have coincided with two major leaders summits being held in Dublin as part of Ireland's EU Presidency. The GRA had accused garda management of breaching working time agreements and of being over-reliant on enforced overtime. Earlier, Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly announced enhanced overtime arrangements for Thursday's European Political Community (EPC) meeting.

stories.title: Behind The Story: Kilkenny chaos and tech honey trap
stories.summary: An influencer boxing event that ended in chaos at the weekend has sparked concern for the city's tourism reputation. The weekend event was organised by social media personality Harrison Sullivan, also known as HSTikkyTokky, who recently featured in Louis Theroux's Netflix documentary Inside the Manosphere. On this episode, Christoper Dunne, Digital Content Editor with the Kilkenny People explains how the controversial event ended up in Kilkenny. The event made headlines after disorder broke out following a confrontation during the event involving social media personality Mo Deen and controversial British activist Tommy Robinson. The disorder spread with several videos showing chaotic scenes inside and outside the event have been prominently shared on social media. One man was taken to hospital. "It was being live streamed on the platform Kick. At last count there were 1.8million viewers." Christoper explains that the venue, the Hub in Cillín Hill, issued a statement after the incident saying that they had a 'zero-tolerance’ policy towards violence, aggression or disorderly behaviour. However, he says concerns have been raised locally about for the impact on Kilkenny’s reputation. "The chair of the local Community Safety Partnership has called for a full garda investigation into the event."

stories.title: Euro zone ministers to discuss ECB appointments
stories.summary: Euro zone finance ministers will today discuss two candidates to replace European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, but are unlikely to make any ⁠recommendations yet, waiting for EU leaders to reach a deal first. Christine Lagarde will step down on February 7, nine months before the end of her term, making the schedule tight because leaders must also fill two other seats on the ECB's Executive Board within months. The two candidates to replace Lagarde are Dutch former central bank governor Klaas Knot and the head of the Bank ‌for International Settlements Pablo Hernandez ⁠de Cos from Spain. Under EU rules, euro zone finance ministers have to recommend a candidate, who then has to have a hearing in the European Parliament before EU leaders make the final appointment. EU governments would like to do that by the ‌end of the year. "We understand that we need to move fast. But what has traditionally happened in the ⁠past is that this was a decision driven by the leaders. ‌Today it will be primarily an information point and the discussion," ⁠the chair ‌of euro zone ministers Kyriakos Pierrakakis told reporters on entering the meeting. Apart from Lagarde, leaders also have to agree on who should replace Isabel Schnabel, the head of the ⁠ECB's marketo perations, who leaves on January 3, 2027, and Chief Economist Philip Lane, ⁠whose term ends in May 2027.

stories.title: Irish captain Sheehan ruled out of Fiji game
stories.summary: Irish captain Dan Sheehan has been ruled out of the side's Nations Championship clash with Fiji on Saturday night. The 28-year-old was forced off for a HIA just before half-time in Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin and never returned to the action. The IRFU confirmed on Monday that Sheehan is undergoing a 12-day return-to-play protocol after suffering a concussion, which takes him out of commission for the meeting with the Fijians on Saturday. Leinster's Gus McCarthy has been called in to train with the squad this week, as has Ulster back row David McCann, who is drafted in to cover the absence of Sean Jansen. Connacht number 8 Jansen has been ruled out of the rest of the championship with a knee injury, picked up early in the second half of Saturday's win. The 27-year-old (below) made his Irish debut against Japan in the summer leg of the Nations Championship, but a knee injury saw him last just 44 minutes against Argentina with Josh van der Flier replacing him. Jansen will now return to his province for rehabilitation.

stories.title: Johnny Depp says he owes his fans for their support
stories.summary: US actor Johnny Depp has said he owes his fans after they supported him "through thick and thin". Depp, 63, stars as the titular character in Ebenezer, a dark fantasy adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol. It marks his first live-action movie role since 2023 and first major return to the big screen since being at the heart of two public trials relating to his ex-wife, actress Amber Heard. In 2022, Depp sued Heard for defamation over a 2018 article she wrote in the Washington Post, which his lawyers said accused him of being an abuser. Jurors returned with a verdict in Depp’s favour. It came after Depp lost a lawsuit in the UK against News Group Newspapers - the owner of The Sun - over an article that called him a "wife beater". A judge ruled in 2020 that the content of the article was proven to be "substantially true".

stories.title: Winners of the 2026 Food & Wine Restaurant of the Year Awards
stories.summary: The 2026 Food&Wine Restaurant of the Year Awards took place last night, celebrating the best of Ireland's hospitality industry. From neighbourhood gems to destination dining, the awards honour outstanding food, service, creativity and consistency across the country. This year's panel of judges consisted of a wide range of journalists and industry experts, including Ali Dunworth, Aoife Carrigy, Bairbre Power, Cathal McBride, Gillian Nelis, Joanne Cronin, Marcus O'Laoire, and the late Corinna Hardgrave, an esteemed restaurant critic who passed away this past October. "My thoughts today are with the women who came forward and made this investigation possible. "Reporting sexual offences can be incredibly difficult, and they have shown immense bravery, dignity and resilience throughout what has been a lengthy investigation and challenging trial process.

stories.title: Raisin issues scam warning over 'physical letter'
stories.summary: Raisin has issued a warning to businesses and its customers in Ireland over what the bank calls a "physical letter" claiming to come from Raisin that is "fake". The German fintech said the letter is "currently circulating in the Irish marketplace". The letter - purporting to come from Raisin - specifically targets businesses, offering them exceptionally high savings rates (above 7.5%) for investments. Such rates would be more than double the best available rates actually available for savers using Raisin and well above the best rates for savers in Ireland. Raisin said the fake documentation was "not issued or authorised" by the company and it advises any businesses receiving it to "not respond, engage, transfer money or disclose personal, business or banking information". The bank said it has alerted the "necessary authorities" to the situation.

stories.title: Carrick on the brink at Man United amid club review
stories.summary: Michael Carrick's days as Manchester United head coach appear to be numbered as the club reviews his position and considers alternatives. The Red Devils will spend the international break in the relegation zone after failing to add to August’s solitary Premier League win against Ipswich in Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. United languish in 18th spot and are reviewing Carrick’s position as the club take stock during the international break. Reports suggest the club intend to replace the former midfielder following talks on Monday, although Old Trafford sources insisted no decision had been made that evening. United director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada seriously considered sacking Carrick a fortnight ago after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth compounded a calamitous 4-1 Champions League loss at Como. The club eventually decided to give the head coach and his players the opportunity to turn the situation around before the international break.

stories.title: Palin says he cannot walk without assistance after fall
stories.summary: Monty Python star Michael Palin has said he still cannot walk without assistance after falling and breaking his ribs at home. The actor, 83, had to cancel a number of events including his In The Philippines travel book tour after a fall in his bathroom in October left him with three broken ribs and a cracked pelvis. Palin shared a health update on Instagram which featured a photograph of him standing in a disabled road bay. He wrote: "It's now exactly a month since I thudded to my bathroom floor - returning from a pee at 3.30 in the morning. I still can’t walk without a zimmer. "The laughs are all on me. Zimmers were used in Monty Python when we wanted to play slow-moving elderly people. "Now I’m an elderly person for real, having to move very slowly as I have three broken ribs and a cracked pelvis. Bones take time to heal and I’m probably doomed to play this particular Python character for a few weeks more."

stories.title: Chef Mark Moriarty: "You rarely get to reflect in this business"
stories.summary: It has been one hell of a year for chef, writer and podcaster, Mark Moriarty, with a new restaurant, a new business hub and a new baby. He talks to Donal O'Donoghue about why his passion for food will never outweigh the priority of family. Last month, Mark Moriarty undertook a literary hike across Dublin, from Chapters bookshop on the northside to Hodges Figgis on the south. It was a rare day off for the chef, writer, podcaster and TV host, so he decided to use those hours by signing his new cookbook, Everyday Delicious, in the capital’s bookshops. It was a job that needed doing, he says, plus he got to meet the booksellers and see the fruits of his labour. "You rarely get to reflect in this business because it’s just forward, forward, forward," he says, adding that at the end of his odyssey, he had a quick lunch (burger and chips), knocked off a radio interview and was home in time for dinner and help put his children to bed. "That was one of the best days of the year because the rest of the time has been absolute chaos". "One hell of a year" is how Moriarty describes 2026 in Everyday Delicious, a year that saw the 34-year-old open his own restaurant (Mark Moriarty Studio), which doubles up as a creative space for his TV shows, podcast, corporate events, photography and consultancy work, and where he employs a staff of eight.

stories.title: Body recovered in Lough Erne in search for missing woman
stories.summary: A body has been recovered from Lough Erne in Co Fermanagh this afternoon during a search for the remains of a Co Limerick woman who has been missing since last month. The body was recovered by a specialist police search team, the PSNI said in a statement. Formal identification of the body has not yet taken place. The body was found in Upper Lough Erne near the village of Carrybridge. The PSNI believes that Carrie Mullane, a 39-year-old mother of four, was killed shortly after arriving in Enniskillen and officers have been searching for her body since being made aware of her disappearance on 29 October. Detective Superintendent Richard Thornton, from the Police Service of Northern Ireland's Serious Crime Branch, said that police have been in contact with her family to inform them of this development and "we continue to provide them with support". "We now must complete the formal identification process which may take a period of time," he said.

stories.title: Small parcels can now be dropped-off via postboxes
stories.summary: From today, customers can post small parcels via postboxes without the need to go into a post office. An Post has announced it is launching a new Postbox Drop-off service. It would mean customers may now send postage-paid small parcels from 2,600 postboxes across the country (out of the total number of 5,300). Consumers will have to print and attach an An Post label to the box, check it in via the app and confirm the posting location. Packages cannot be larger than 240mm x 45mm, and should never be left on or beside a postbox. If an item does not drop easily into the postbox, it should be brought to any post office. Introducing the new feature, An Post noted that the large number of parcels posted with print-at-home, postage-paid labels are small in size, containing small accessories, books, single garments or other small items which can fit easily into some postboxes.

stories.title: Could viral hair hacks be damaging your hair?
stories.summary: The likes of TikTok and Instagram have tried to convince us that growing thicker, longer and healthier hair is simply a matter of finding the right ingredient. Rosemary oil supposedly stimulates your follicles, scalp massagers allegedly encourage growth, and collagen shampoos promise to leave you with a fuller head of hair, while we're also told that washing your hair less frequently can train it to become less greasy. But how much of this viral advice is actually supported by science? Some are fact, some are fiction. Trichologist Anabel Kingsley, whose new book, Haircare: The Ultimate Guide, explores the relationship between women's health and hair, says it's important to distinguish between the trends and treatments that are actually backed by scientific evidence. So here's a breakdown of what the most popular hair hacks actually do to your scalp and hair – and whether they're worth trying. Rosemary oil has managed to enjoy great PR online, from scalp-oiling tutorials to elaborate overnight routines; it's often promoted as a natural alternative to chemical hair-loss treatments.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth to face expected impeachment vote this week
stories.summary: A Republican politician has moved to impeach US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting up a potentially explosive vote in Congress just days after President Donald Trump's party suffered a crushing midterm defeat. Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment accusing Mr Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. The Republican-controlled House could vote as early as Wednesday, with some politicians from Mr Trump's party signalling that they might join Democrats in supporting the charges. Impeachment would be a humiliating blow for Mr Hegseth and the Trump administration, but would not automatically remove him from office. That would require a trial and conviction by a two-thirds majority in the Senate -- a far higher hurdle, even after Democrats take control of the chamber in January. The impeachment push has gathered momentum since Tuesday's midterm elections, when Democrats swept both chambers of Congress amid widespread anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel prices.

stories.title: Western railway platform extensions expected next year
stories.summary: Extensions of railway station platforms between Limerick and Athenry in Co Galway are expected to be completed by the end of the next year, as part of an effort to boost passenger capacity on the route. Iarnród Éireann is issuing tender documents for the construction works at five stations today. This will allow for six carriage trains to stop at Sixmilebridge, Ennis, Gort, Ardrahan and Craughwell. Platforms will be extended by 55 metres at four of the stations, with a 12 metre enhancement planned for Ennis. Iarnród Éireann said track enabling works are already under way and that it hopes to award a contract to the successful applicant by the end of the year. Chief Executive Mary Considine said the initiative will increase capacity and broaden transport options for those living close to the Galway - Limerick rail line.

stories.title: Brady quits role as Birmingham City minority owner
stories.summary: NFL legend Tom Brady has relinquished his minority share in Sky Bet Championship leaders Birmingham City after three years with the club. The seven-time Super Bowl winner bought a stake in the club as part of the 2023 takeover by the Knighthead group, headed by his friend and business partner Tom Wagner. But Brady has chosen to step away despite Blues moving to the top of the table two days ago with a 2-1 win over Swansea at St Andrew's. "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years," the club said in a statement. "It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community." Birmingham have expressed big ambitions on and off the pitch. Wagner has indicated his desire to reach the Premier League, while plans are in place for a new 62,000-capacity stadium in the city.

stories.title: Faulkner would not have recovered from attack, court told
stories.summary:
A trial at the Central Criminal Court has heard that 28-year-old Scarlett Faulkner would never have recovered from injuries sustained in an attack on the roadside at Birdhill last March. The 28-year-old died on 13 April after suffering a severe brain injury the previous month. State Pathologist Margaret Bolster was giving evidence on the fifth day of the trial of a 41-year-old woman and a 17-year-old girl who deny the charge of murder. The teenager has admitted manslaughter, but the prosecution says both accused were part of a joint enterprise which led to the murder of Ms Faulkner. Neither of the accused can be named to protect the anonymity of the teenager.

Dr Bolster told the jury that Ms Faulkner had died as a result of a severe, traumatic brain injury caused by multiple forceful blows with a blunt weapon. She said the injuries were consistent with multiple blows from something like an iron bar shown to her by gardaí.

stories.title: Bohs lure Hakiki from Sligo for 2027
stories.summary: Bohemians have made their first signing for the 2027 League of Ireland season, with Jad Hakiki joining from Sligo Rovers. Hakiki has signed a two-year deal with the Phibsborough club having previously spent time with Shelbourne and Dundalk. The 22-year-old also has 10 U21 caps for Ireland as he makes the move to the side who finished second in this campaign, three points behind eventual winners Shamrock Rovers. "I'm delighted to be here, and I’m really looking forward to trying to kick on," he said in a statement. "I’ve spoken to the manager and have heard the ambitions for the club going forward and what they want to do next year. "It all really appealed to me, so I couldn’t wait to sign. Bohs had a really good season, have kept the core of the group here, so I want to come in and knuckle down, progress and help push the club on further.

stories.title: US seeing 'strong inclination' Ukraine war to end - Trump
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has said that Washington was seeing a "very strong inclination" towards ending Russia's war in Ukraine and that both sides were "tired of fighting." "We're having a very good conversation about that in Abu Dhabi," Mr Trump told reporters at the White House on the eve of US-led, three-sided talks scheduled in Abu Dhabi. Mr Trump had vowed to end the conflict when he took office in January 2025 but the goal to end the war that began with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 has remained elusive. "We're also seeing a very strong inclination to end Russia and Ukraine (war). We're involved in that," Mr Trump said. Both Russia and Ukraine were showing some flexibility privately on the possible exchange of territory ahead of the talks in Abu Dhabi this week, a US official said. The official, briefing reporters ahead of talks that begin tomorrow, said security guarantees for Ukraine will be a major topic for the discussions, including the potential for a NATO-style Article 5 defence for Kyiv.

stories.title: Portmarnock must wait as Carnoustie set to host 2029 Open
stories.summary: Portmarnock Golf Club's attempt to host the Open Championship will extend into at least the next decade as Carnoustie was confirmed as the venue for the 2029 event. It will be the first time in 11 years that the Scottish links will host the major with Italian Francesco Molinari winning in Angus with two shots to spare over a group that included County Down's Rory McIlroy. The Open has been staged in Ireland three times – all at Royal Portrush in County Antrim – and in July, hopes grew that Portmarnock would be added to the rota. Mark Darbon, chief executive of the R&A, revealed that discussions with all key stakeholders – including the Government – were at an advanced stage. "It's a complicated venue because of the scale of The Open Championship so there's been a lot of great feasibility work with the golf club themselves, with the local authority, with government. We've undertaken a big feasibility study. "That work is pretty much done. We've confirmed that we believe we can take an Open Championship there,"

stories.title: Lindsay Clancy loses bid to dismiss murder charges
stories.summary: A Massachusetts judge has cleared the way for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again on murder charges for killing her three young children at her home in 2023, saying a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject her to a double prosecution for the same crime. Judge William Sullivan in Plymouth rejected a bid by Ms Clancy's attorneys to have the case against her dismissed. The judge on 4 September declared a mistrial after the jury reported that a holdout juror was preventing it from reaching a unanimous verdict. The judge has scheduled a 26 November hearing to discuss when to hold a second trial, which he has suggested could occur in March. No one at Ms Clancy's initial trial disputed that she strangled daughter Cora, 5; son Dawson, 3; and 8-month-old son Callan on 24 January, 2023, in the basement of their home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury. She then attempted to end her own life, leaving her paralysed. Her lawyers have argued that Ms Clancy was in the throes of postpartum psychosis and should be found not guilty by reason of insanity, known in Massachusetts as lack of criminal responsibility.

stories.title: Scales enjoying Celtic's focus on setpieces
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland international Liam Scales is enjoying Celtic's renewed focus on making setpieces count after volleying home the winner against Kilmarnock at the weekend to take his tally for the season to three. "I don’t really have a target for goals – it’s more about clean sheets for me," the 28-year-old said. "But it’s nice. "It is nice to score and hopefully I can get a few more between now and the end of the season." He also backed teammate Kasper Hogh to get back in the scoring books. The striker has had a barren spell with Scales now level on goals with him this season. Hogh had a goal disallowed for an earlier foul in Saturday’s 1-0 win over Kilmarnock to make it 16 matches since he netted a hat-trick at Rugby Park in his second appearance since joining Celtic for a club-record £11m.

stories.title: France says Iran behind 'unprecedented' cyberattacks
stories.summary: France has said Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind cyberattacks on supermarket fridges in the country last month, vowing sanctions on a European level against Tehran over the first such large-scale cyber sabotage on French territory. Numerous French supermarkets were hit in the 11 and 12 October cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators, in some cases forcing them to throw away entire inventories of perishable food. "I can confirm that this attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of the Islamic Republic of Iran," Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said of the cyberattacks. "This attack is unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression," he said on the sidelines of the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris. The Paris prosecutor said in a separate statement she had opened an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, a shadowy cyber unit of the IRGC, the Islamic republic's ideological army, over the attacks. The cyber monitoring centre of four French security agencies said the unit is better known in the cyber world as CyberAveng3rs, its avatar through which it has claimed attacks in the past.

stories.title: Cancer treatment prompts Biden to reduce memoir promotion
stories.summary: Former US president Joe Biden says he is scaling back plans to promote his upcoming memoir as he undergoes treatment for aggressive prostate cancer, acknowledging that the illness sometimes leaves him struggling. The 83-year-old Democrat, whose cognitive decline was a major issue during his presidency and ultimately ended his bid to stay in power, has said that he would be unable to make as many public appearances as he had hoped ahead of the 17 November release of "Promise Me, America." "Some days are better than others. It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down," Mr Biden wrote on X. "What that means is, unfortunately, I won't be able to do as many conversations about my book as I'd hoped. However, I'm hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves." Mr Biden announced in May 2025, four months after leaving the White House, that he had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had spread to his bones. He has since undergone radiation and hormone therapy, while his son Hunter said in August that the disease had spread further and was causing considerable pain.

stories.title: Cork to kick off Division 1 title defence at Waterford
stories.summary: Cork will begin the defence of their Lidl National Football League Division 1 crown with a visit to Waterford on the opening weekend of the 2027 campaign. The all-Munster clash, scheduled for Saturday, 23 January at 12pm, will be televised live by TG4. The following day – Sunday, 24 January – All-Ireland champions Galway host Kerry in what is a repeat of this year's All-Ireland final. Elsewhere in Division 1 on the same day, an all-Ulster clash sees Armagh entertain newly-promoted Donegal, while promoted Cavan make the trip to neighbours Meath. Round 2 will feature two provincial derbies, with both games live on TG4 on Monday, 1 February. Cavan host Donegal at 2pm, followed by Cork’s home fixture with Kerry at 3.45pm.

stories.title: Media watchdog investigation into two radio stations
stories.summary: Coimisiún na Meán has launched separate "formal broadcasting investigations" into South East Radio and Tipp FM. The media regulator has said the investigations will assess suspected contraventions of the Broadcasting Act 2009 and the broadcasting codes. A spokesperson for Coimisiún na Meán has said the investigations have commenced following complaints assessed and processed through its broadcasting and video-on-demand complaint process. The spokesperson said: "As a result of these complaints, concerns arose regarding suspected contraventions of both statutory provisions of the Broadcasting Act 2009 (as amended) and regulatory provisions of the broadcasting codes". Coimisiún na Meán has said it will investigate whether South East Radio breached the Code of Fairness, Objectivity and Impartiality in News and Current Affairs, in addition to sections of the Broadcasting Act 2009 (as amended) concerning news and current affairs. The media regulator will separately investigate whether Tipp FM breached the Code of Programme Standards and the Code of Fairness, Objectivity and Impartiality in News and Current Affairs.

stories.title: The cautionary tale of the disappearing town
stories.summary: As world leaders gather in Turkey for COP31 this week, support for countries hardest hit by climate change will be high on the agenda. Among those nations is Honduras, where extreme weather and rising sea levels are increasingly threatening communities. Reporter Kate Varley and cameraman Bram Verbeke travelled to the Central American country to hear from those on the frontlines of the crisis. When you ask the people of Cedeño to describe the town they've called home for decades, one word comes up time and again: paradise. Nestled between sandy beaches and lush forests, this community on Honduras' Pacific coast looks like it belongs on a glossy postcard. Cedeño is fighting for its survival, and month by month it is losing a battle to the advancing sea - turning what was once a slice of paradise into a source of despair for residents.
